Empirical Research Plan  
“Banking‐sector development, growth, and the TFP-vs-capital accumulation debate”

-------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------------
• Strategy: Cross-country two-stage least-squares (2SLS) / IV estimation that uses exogenous variation in national legal origin to instrument for banking-sector development.  
• Why IV?  
  – Endogeneity of banking depth: growth prospects can themselves attract financial deepening (reverse causality); both may be driven by omitted third factors (e.g., cultural norms, geography).  
  – Legal origin is (i) predetermined (assigned by colonial conquest or occupation, largely prior to 20th-century growth) and (ii) shown to affect creditor rights, information disclosure, and therefore the size/efficiency of financial intermediation.  
• Complementary analyses:  
  – Panel 2SLS with country and period fixed effects to exploit within-country growth episodes.  
  – “Channels” regressions that replace the growth outcome with TFP growth, capital accumulation, or private saving to test mechanisms.

-------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable (endogenous regressor)  
  • BANKDEV_ct: one of the three measures, baseline = Private Credit / GDP (PCREDIT).

Instrument(s) (Z_c, time-invariant)  
  • LEGAL_ENGLISH, LEGAL_FRENCH, LEGAL_GERMAN, LEGAL_SCAND (English common law is the omitted category).  
  • Optionally, creditor-rights score of La Porta et al. (1998) to strengthen relevance.  

Control group / counterfactual  
  • Countries whose legal origin predicts systematically lower banking depth (e.g., French civil-law origin) act as “controls” for high-bank-depth common-law countries.

Timing  
  • Legal origin determined centuries ago ⇒ no timing variation; IV relies on cross-sectional assignment.  
  • In the panel, BANKDEV varies every 5 years; the instrument remains constant.

Treatment–control interpretation  
  • 2SLS coefficient gives the causal effect of an exogenously predicted change in banking depth (coming from legal origin) on growth.

-------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------------
A1. Relevance – Legal origin is strongly correlated with BANKDEV (first-stage F ≫ 10).  
     Plausible: abundant prior evidence.

A2. Exclusion – Legal origin affects long-run growth only through the banking channel, not through other independent channels once we condition on standard covariates (human capital, trade openness, inflation, government size, etc.).  
     Plausibility: Debatable because legal origin shapes broader institutions; we mitigate via rich controls and mechanism checks.

A3. Independence – Legal origin is quasi-random with respect to countries’ unobservable growth determinants after controls (e.g., geography, natural resources).  
     Plausibility: Reasonable; colonizers did not choose legal codes based on today’s growth prospects.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA) – One country’s legal origin does not directly affect another’s growth via spillovers beyond global price effects (small-open-economy assumption).  
     Plausibility: High.

A5. Linearity & homogeneous effect – The marginal effect of BANKDEV on growth is constant across the instrument-induced range.  
     Plausibility: Acceptable, but we will test for non-linearities (e.g., interaction with income level).

-------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
-------------------------------------------------------
T1. Exclusion violation via “broader institutions”  
   • Remedy:  
     – Control for rule-of-law, corruption, property-rights, and educational attainment indices.  
     – Over-identification tests (Hansen J) using multiple legal-origin dummies.  
     – Conduct “plausibly exogenous” sensitivity bounds (Conley et al., 2012).

T2. Weak instrument in sub-samples (e.g., post-1980)  
   • Remedy: report first-stage F-statistics, use LIML/Fuller(1) as robustness, drop weakly forecasted regions.

T3. Measurement error in BANKDEV or growth components  
   • Remedy: rely on multiple banking indicators; errors-in-variables bias in OLS turns into attenuation, IV corrects if instrument does not share measurement error.

-------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------------
```r
#--- 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # fast demeaned 2SLS
library(modelsummary) # nice tables
library(sandwich)    # robust vcov
library(lmtest)

#--- 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
cross  <- read_csv("data_cross_averages.csv")   # 63 x-section
panel  <- read_csv("data_panel_5yr.csv")        # 77 × 7 = 539 obs

#--- 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
cross <- cross %>%
  mutate(
    g_gdp     = gdp_pc_growth,                   # outcome
    tfp       = tfp_growth_solow,
    g_k       = k_pc_growth,
    s_priv    = private_saving_rate,
    bankdev   = private_credit_gdp,
    lny0      = log(gdp_pc_1960),
    school60  = schooling_1960,
    open      = trade_gdp,
    gov       = gov_consumption_gdp,
    infl      = inflation_cpi,
    bmprem    = black_market_premium,
    # Legal origin dummies (English omitted)
    lg_french = if_else(legal=="FRENCH",1,0),
    lg_germ   = if_else(legal=="GERMAN",1,0),
    lg_scan   = if_else(legal=="SCAND",1,0)
  )

#--- 3. Baseline 2SLS ---------------------------------------------------------
iv_baseline <- feols(g_gdp ~ bankdev + lny0 + school60 + open + gov + infl + bmprem |
                       lg_french + lg_germ + lg_scan,
                     data = cross, vcov = "hetero")

summary(iv_baseline)

#--- 4. Mechanism regressions -------------------------------------------------
iv_tfp <- feols(tfp ~ bankdev + lny0 + school60 + ... |
                  lg_french + lg_germ + lg_scan, data = cross, vcov = "hetero")

iv_cap <- feols(g_k ~ bankdev + controls |
                  lg_french + lg_germ + lg_scan, data = cross, vcov = "hetero")

iv_sav <- feols(s_priv ~ bankdev + controls |
                  lg_french + lg_germ + lg_scan, data = cross, vcov = "hetero")

#--- 5. Over-identification test & weak-IV diagnostics ------------------------
wald_iv <- wald_iv(iv_baseline)      # first-stage F
ivreg::summary(iv_baseline, diagnostics = TRUE)

#--- 6. Panel robustness: within-country fixed effects ------------------------
panel <- panel %>% mutate(period = factor(period))

iv_panel <- feols(g_gdp ~ bankdev + lny0 + school + open + gov + infl + bmprem |
                    . ~ (lg_french + lg_germ + lg_scan) ,
                  data = panel,
                  fixef = ~ country + period,
                  vcov = "cluster")

#--- 7. Sensitivity: alternative banker measure -------------------------------
cross$bank_liab <- liquid_liabilities_gdp

iv_liab <- feols(g_gdp ~ bank_liab + controls | lg_french + lg_germ + lg_scan,
                 data = cross, vcov = "hetero")

modelsummary(list(PCredit = iv_baseline, Liab = iv_liab))
```

-------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------------
Theory predicts a positive effect: deeper banking systems ease allocation of capital to high-return projects, foster creative destruction, and thereby raise long-run growth mainly through TFP, with a secondary effect on capital accumulation. Magnitude guess: a 30 pp (=1 sd) increase in Private Credit/GDP should raise annual per-capita growth by roughly 1 percentage point; about 60–70 % of this would operate via faster TFP growth.

-------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV design)
-------------------------------------------------------
C1: Strong first stage (F > 10) .................... 1  
C2: Exclusion restriction believable ............... 0.5  
C3: Independence / as-good-as-random assignment .... 0.8  
C4: No treatment spillovers (SUTVA) ................ 1  
C5: Correct functional form / monotonicity ......... 0.8  

Total ≈ 4.1 / 5.
